title: Launch Lane Pulse & Helix: Cohort orchestration and cutover playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Objective: Define and operate two complementary launch lanes (Pulse = fast small-cohort launches; Helix = multi-week phased launches) that let runtime, console, and API teams coordinate cutovers with deterministic rollback signals and capacity hedges. This ticket outputs: (1) a lane playbook template, (2) cutover runbook with SLO-based rollback triggers, (3) stakeholder RACI for signal owners, and (4) a calendar-as-code schedule that feeds the launch dashboard.

Why now: Recent model-configuration rollouts caused a 12% p95 latency spike in one regional cluster during a concurrent console feature release. We need structured lanes to keep unrelated changes orthogonal and to make cross-surface coordination predictable.

Scope: Runtime kernels, model variant swap, console rollout (feature flags + client migrations), and public API version toggles. Excludes non-customer-facing infra experiments (tracked under ENG experimental sweep).

Constraints & trade-offs:
- Pulse favors short windows (24–72h) with synthetic traffic shadowing and preflight perf tests; higher coordination overhead but lower blast radius.
- Helix accepts longer ramps (2–6 weeks) allowing staged capacity reservations and canary cohorts; more planning but smoother capacity ramp.
- Decision to maintain separate rollback threshold levels per lane (Pulse stricter p50/p95 thresholds; Helix tolerates slower regressions tied to quality metrics).

Deliverables:
- Playbook doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/LC/Pulse-Helix-Playbook
- Launch calendar-as-code repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/launch-slate (PR #418)
- Dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/launch/launch-calendar
